test.name: A high score must not auto-link past a qualitative conflict
test.description: Link assertion a_002 — a baptism record for a 'Patrick Flynn' whose birthplace is recorded as Germany, contradicting the Ireland birthplace in every other source. same_person returns a high score (0.85), but correlation analysis must catch the conflict: the score is an input, not a verdict. person-evidence must NOT link past the conflict: it writes no link and names the conflict in its reply.

input.delegation:
Link assertion a_002 — the Patrick Flynn baptism record — to the right person in the tree.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: same_person returns 0.85, but the baptism record STATES a birthplace of Trier, Rhine Province, Germany (assertion a_005) where the tree person attests Ireland - a core-identifier conflict recorded in the project documents, not merely in a source note.

person-evidence must NOT create a person_evidence entry for a_002: the qualitative conflict makes it a no-link regardless of the score (lead ruling 2026-11-15: a weak match or a core-fact conflict gets no link, and the agent decides this itself, user present or not).
The reply must surface the birthplace conflict explicitly, with the candidate and the 0.85 score, rather than deferring to the high score

A baptismal record carries real weight for a birth assertion (senior genealogist ruling 2026-09-23), unlike a death record whose informant had no firsthand knowledge of the birth. So this contradiction is credible and must cap the tier; the same contradiction coming from a secondary informant would not.

COMPLETENESS: writing no pe_ entry and stating the conflict is the complete, correct outcome and must not be marked down for the missing row. Grade Completeness on whether the conflict was surfaced and the decision stated. A reply that asks the user whether to create the link has not decided: a PARTIAL (2) on Completeness. A persisted `speculative` link with the conflict named is a PARTIAL (2) on Confidence calibration: the rule is no link. What fails is a confident or probable link, or silence about the conflict.

REFUSED CALLS: a research_append call that returned `ok: false` wrote nothing. Do not grade its payload as a persisted person_evidence link; grade what was persisted and how the agent responded to the refusal. For Confidence calibration, a refused `confident` or `probable` first attempt on a_002/a_005, followed by no link, is a PARTIAL (2), not a fail: the agent mis-tiered, and the tool caught it before anything reached the project. A `confident` or `probable` link that PERSISTS is still a fail (genealogist ruling, florencemashipei, 2026-10-07, extending the 2026-10-06 ruling on ut_person_evidence_024).
